newsitem.title: USA: Recycling restates Q3 to show wider loss.
newsitem.headline: Recycling restates Q3 to show wider loss.

text.p: Recycling Industries Inc said Tuesday it was restating its results for the third quarter ended June 30, increasing its operating loss by $628,000 to $1,148,000.
The company said the restated operating loss brought its third-quarter net loss to $1,126,000, or $0.10 per share, and resulted in an $0.11 per share loss for the first nine months.
It had previously reported per-share losses of $0.05 and $0.04 for the three-month and nine-month periods, respectively.

The company also said Brian Klemsz joined the company as chief financial officer and a director, succeeding Jerry Misukanis, who stepped down as chief financial officer because of health problems. Misukanis will remain a director.
Recycling said it expected to post record revenue in the fourth quarter while operations at the plant level were likely to break even.

Recycling, a full-service metal recycler, said it was restating its third-quarter results to reflect changes in accounting estimates used to value inventory at its Texas facility, acquired in December 1995.
It also said the increased loss stemmed from adjustments to accounts receivable at its Nevada facility and adjustments to depreciation and goodwill.
The company said the need for restatement surfaced during the preparation for the company's year-end audit.

Noting that third-quarter revenue rose 84 percent to $6,721,000, Recycling said July was a record month for revenue. The company said it thought the positive trend continued during the fourth quarter.
Klemsz will oversee the implementation of additional systems and improved controls throughout the company, Recycling said.
Before joining the company, he served in various financial and systems management positions for eight years with Advanced Energy Industries Inc.
